Punchline: Community language localizer. Needs a language pack.
Description:
Gubal Library hands the game pre-translated copies of its own text files, so the game draws another language itself, in its own font and its own layout. Nothing is overlaid and your install is never touched.

It ships empty and belongs to no language: point it at a community language pack and the game speaks that language. You choose what gets translated and what stays English, part by part.

/gubal → Opens the settings window.
/gubal status → What is installed, what is being served, and whether it reached the game.
/gubal parts → Lists what the pack covers and what you have switched off.
/gubal check → Asks the publisher whether a newer pack exists.
/gubal usepack → Serves the installed pack, or stops serving it.
/gubal autoupdate → Fetches a newer pack while the game is starting.
/gubal probesqpack → Diagnostics for when a page is not reaching the game.

A pack must match the patch you are running, and the game reads its text once at startup, so a change takes effect the next time you start the client.

This is a testing build. Please report problems on GitHub.

//LoadRequiredState: 2 means 'no requirement', which is the EARLIEST of Dalamud's three load stages, not the
latest — 0 is 'when drawing facilities are available' and is the default. Left at the default,
this plugin loaded in the last batch, five seconds after the game had already begun reading
its Excel sheets, so any page redirection it registered arrived too late to matter. Measured:
LoadPluginsSync(AnytimeSync) ended 15:05:56.407, 'Boot load started' 15:05:56.408, and this
This alone is enough, and that matters because the alternative was asking every user to change
a Dalamud setting. An earlier note here claimed 'Wait for plugins before game loads' was also
required; measured 2026-08-08 with that setting OFF, the read hook still installed 2.1s ahead
of the client's first Excel read and the boot-loaded sheets came out Spanish. The setting was
on during the run that established this line, which is the only reason it looked necessary.
